Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
- Presentation: 3-day history of watery diarrhoea every ~10 min, central abdominal cramps relieved by stooling, one episode of vomiting, no blood, minimal oral intake, no documented fever.  
- Most consistent with acute infectious gastroenteritis (likely viral; DDx high likelihood). Bacterial food-borne gastroenteritis also possible (moderate likelihood).  
- Less likely: IBS/post-infectious functional change, IBD, or colorectal cancer (short course, lack of red-flag features).  
- Dehydration risk given poor oral intake; no current red-flag features (no blood, severe pain, persistent vomiting, high fever).  
- Plan discussed:  • Increase oral fluids/electrolytes  • Monitor for fever, blood in stool/vomit, worsening pain, or inability to hydrate  • Remain off work/home rest until improving  • Avoid empiric antibiotics  • Seek in-person GP review if symptoms worsen or not improving within 24-48 h  

Management Plan
- management_plan_main_or_not_recorded: As above—supportive management with hydration, monitoring for red-flags, GP follow-up if no improvement/worse. No medications prescribed. NKDA documented.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
1. Acute infectious gastroenteritis – likely viral (High): Sudden onset, watery diarrhoea, brief vomiting, abdominal cramps, no blood/fever.  
2. Bacterial food-borne gastroenteritis (Moderate): Similar symptom cluster; exposure history unclear; lack of fever or blood slightly less supportive.  
3. Colorectal carcinoma (Low): Family history, but acute presentation and absence of chronic red-flags make this unlikely.
